words.macro: The week's move is a supply-disruption story: vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply as Iran targets tankers defying its demands, and Washington's escalating threats kept a war premium in the price. Front-month WTI settled above $86 on 20 August, its highest in over two weeks, with the pressure feeding straight into equity-market inflation worry.
words.long_term: OPEC+ completed the rollback of its voluntary cuts with September's scheduled increase, so the structural question into 2027 is whether restored supply or Gulf disruption risk dominates; the strait remains the single largest scheduled-to-nothing risk in the complex.

eoy_scenarios.central: The Hormuz premium ebbs and flows without a supply break; restored OPEC+ barrels cap rallies and WTI churns inside the script's central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: An actual interruption of strait volumes — not threats — repricing the barrel well above the band's top; this is the fat tail the 80% envelope deliberately leaves out.
eoy_scenarios.downside: De-escalation drains the war premium while the completed cut rollback leaves the market amply supplied into year-end.
